frameworks.name: Open-Gate Product Selection Framework
frameworks.definition: Choose the next product by identifying where your unique asset stack (relationships, capital, team capabilities) makes an apparently impossible barrier into an open gate that competitors cannot walk through.

claims.text: Greg Lavecchia and his wife bootstrapped Bloom Nutrition from founding to $180 million in annual revenue between ages 27 and 30 (a roughly three-year window), demonstrating that CPG/DTC supplement businesses can reach that revenue level without external venture capital when founders combine retail distribution relationships, manufacturing capabilities, and brand marketing competency.
claims.speaker: Greg Lavecchia
conditions: Founders hold pre-existing retailer and distribution relationships
Founders have in-house formulation and manufacturing access
Founders have a team capable of brand marketing at scale

numbers.axis: revenue growth timeline by founder age

bounded_by: Lavecchia does not claim this growth rate is achievable without the specific asset stack (retailer relationships, distribution, capital access, brand/manufacturing team)

claims.text: Greg Lavecchia asserts that the optimal product selection criterion is identifying where your unique capabilities make what appears publicly to be an impossible barrier into an open gate: a product category so difficult for most entrants that the barrier itself filters out competitors, but where your specific asset stack removes that barrier for you. For Bloom Sparkling Energy (launched 2024), Lavecchia's team's retailer relationships, distribution access, capital, and brand-marketing-plus-formulation team constituted this open gate.
claims.speaker: Greg Lavecchia
conditions: Entrepreneur is selecting a new product category to enter in a competitive wellness or CPG market
Entrepreneur has accumulated specific assets from prior business that are non-replicable by most new entrants
claims.mechanism: A high barrier to entry that filters most competitors becomes a competitive moat for the entrant who already possesses the assets that dissolve that barrier; the barrier that looks like a wall to others is an open gate to those with the right capabilities, making the category simultaneously defensible and accessible.
bounded_by: Does not apply to entrepreneurs without accumulated differentiated asset stacks; in that case the barrier filters them out too

claims.text: Greg Lavecchia contends that entrepreneurs should apply the open-gate criterion when deciding which product to release in any given year: the question is not what product they can make, but what product would be considered impossible by nearly everyone else yet achievable by them given their unique capabilities.
claims.speaker: Greg Lavecchia
conditions: Applies to entrepreneurs with existing businesses who are deciding whether and what to extend into
claims.mechanism: Pursuing what appears impossible to others — but is possible given your asset stack — creates a moat that is structural rather than incremental, because competitors are pre-filtered by the barrier you can walk through.

examples.text: In 2024, Greg Lavecchia and his wife decided to launch Bloom Sparkling Energy after identifying it as a product that met the open-gate criterion. The wellness/CPG category for sparkling energy drinks had high barriers to entry: retailer relationships, distribution infrastructure, formulation and manufacturing capability, capital, and a brand-marketing team. Lavecchia's team had all of these from building Bloom Nutrition. What appeared to outside entrepreneurs as an impossible market to penetrate — high retailer gatekeeping, complex supply chain, competitive shelf space — was an open gate for the Lavecchias because their existing asset stack neutralized every barrier.

practices.text: When planning a new product launch, audit your unique assets (existing relationships, team capabilities, capital, distribution access) and use them as the filter for which opportunities to pursue — target categories where your assets dissolve barriers that would stop nearly anyone else.
